title: Volume of Prisms
short: V = Bh for any prism, where B is the area of the base.
trouble: Students use the area of the side face as B instead of the base that matches the height.

blocks.html: You know that a box's volume is $V = lwh$, even with fractional edges. That rule is part of a bigger one that works for every prism, including prisms with triangle bases.
For any right prism, $V = Bh$. $B$ is the area of the base, the face that is the same all the way through the prism, and $h$ is the distance between the two bases.

Slice a prism into layers 1 unit thick, parallel to the base. Each layer is a copy of the base, so each holds $B$ cubic units. There are $h$ layers, so the volume is $B \times h$. For a box, the base is a rectangle, $B = lw$, and $V = lwh$ is the same rule.

blocks.title: A box with a fraction
blocks.q: Find the volume of a box $2\frac{1}{2}$ ft long, 4 ft wide and 3 ft tall.

blocks.title: A triangular prism
blocks.q: The prism above has triangle bases with base 10 in. and height 6 in. It is 9 in. long. Find its volume.
steps: The base is the triangle: $B = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30$ square in.

blocks.title: Finding a height
blocks.q: A fish tank holds 360 cubic inches. Its base is 9 in. by 8 in. How tall is it?

blocks.html: Using a rectangular side face as the base of a triangular prism. The base is the face that stays the same shape all the way through, here the triangle. Check: in $V = Bh$, $h$ must be the distance between the two bases, which is the prism's length.
